title: Photography
text:
As a wizard and scholar of Middle-earth, I have been studying the magic of the natural world for centuries. Through my self-portraits, I aim to capture the essence of my own being and reflect on my own journey through time. Each photograph is a reflection of my own experiences and emotions. Through my photography, I hope to offer a glimpse into my life as a scholar and adventurer, and inspire others to reflect on their own journeys through the world.

title: Projects
text:
arXiv Preprint | Code
Over the centuries, I have devoted countless hours to deciphering and translating the ancient scripts and dialects of the various peoples of Middle-earth. My goal is to gain a deeper understanding of the cultures and histories of these peoples by studying their languages. Currently, I am working on a monograph that explores the linguistic roots of the Elvish languages. Through extensive research and analysis, I hope to shed light on the connections between the different dialects of Elvish and their origins. This project has been particularly challenging, as Elvish is a complex and nuanced language, but I am determined to see it through to completion.

section: The History of the War of the Ring
text:
The History of the War of the Ring

arXiv Preprint | Code
I am creating a comprehensive and detailed history of the conflict that goes beyond the surface-level events. By gathering information from a variety of sources, including my own memories, written accounts, and oral histories, I hope to shed new light on this important period in Middle-earth’s history and provide valuable insights into the motivations and actions of the various players involved.

Welcome
I’m Catherine C. Osborn, a Bioinformatics Research Associate with Special Technical Skills at the Prevention Research Center for Healthy Neighborhoods (PRCHN) at Case Western Reserve University. Most of my work involves building the data systems that community health research depends on, from REDCap databases for clinical trials to automated reporting for quality improvement projects. I’m also a PhD student in Clinical Translational Science at CWRU, where my focus is on how interventions that work in research settings get carried into everyday clinical and community practice.


Experience
I’ve worked at the PRCHN since 2016, developing data collection instruments, protocols, and databases for studies on prostate cancer screening, rural environmental health, and community health interventions. I’ve led large-scale surveys on youth health behaviors in Cuyahoga and Summit Counties, and as a contractor for the Ohio Youth Risk Behavior Survey. I also built the data collection platform for the Cleveland Health Survey and helped develop new methods for tracking emerging tobacco products. My analytic work covers chronic health conditions, substance use, tobacco use disparities, and cancer screening, and I’m an author on ten peer-reviewed publications.


Current Projects
Nourishing Tomorrow: a food as medicine trial providing medically tailored groceries to food-insecure pregnant women at MetroHealth and University Hospitals. I designed the study’s data systems across both hospital sites and work with community health workers on enrollment and oversee data collection by study staff and community partners.
Healthy Futures Research Study: a project looking at the potential health impact of the chemical exposure following the 2023 train derailment in East Palestine, Ohio. I’ve built the study’s data infrastructure and overseen data collection protocols related to health surveys, behavioral assessments, and at-home biospecimen collection.
Pike Moore Lab: For Dr. Stephanie Pike Moore, I’m developing the platform for an ecological momentary assessment (EMA) study and network maps of companies behind emerging hemp-derived cannabinoids and other unregulated psychoactive products.
